value: The Ashen Hand has struck twice near the Merrow road, raiding two homesteads and stealing their stores. One family lost its roof to the storm that followed, a common enough fate for those left behind in the open. Travelers know this well now: caravans move only in pairs, doubled with guards, accepting that the cost of safety is higher than the profit of haste. The Merrow Freeholds have adapted, but they cannot stop the firebrand from crossing their path again tomorrow. Kinn scouts say grass fires south will shift their tracks north soon; they offer no intent to fight, though I doubt anyone else cares for peace when the wind blows hard enough to set everything alight.

- Merrow Freeholds caravans now travel only in pairs

## Your earlier bulletins

The Ashen Hand are out in numbers. Two homesteads on the Merrow road lost their stores, and one lost its roof. Merrow traders are travelling in pairs now, which doubles the guards and, they assure me, the prices.

Latest bulletin:
Grass fires in the south have the Kinn on the move. They are not, by their account, looking for trouble. Neither, I suspect, is trouble looking for them, but it usually finds someone.

attempts.text: Day 23 at Kettle Hollow. The Ashen Hand expanded its footprint today, raiding two additional homesteads along the Merrow road. It has become a matter of survival; all Freehold caravans are now traveling in pairs to avoid becoming targets for their growing band. Meanwhile, the fires continue to scorch the southern reaches, pushing the Kinn toward new grazing grounds. They insist they seek only pasture, not conflict, though one rarely believes their own assurances when smoke rises from the north. The Rim grows hotter, both in temperature and in tension. If you are crossing these lines, pray your goods do not match those stolen in the last few weeks.
